background: Mizuho Financial Group is one of Japan's three megabanks, the holding company of Mizuho Bank and Mizuho Securities, funded by a very large base of yen deposits and lending to Japanese corporates and households and to large companies worldwide.
synthesis: Two of the three main agencies rate the group, A- on average, both on a stable outlook, with no move since a one-notch downgrade by one of the three on 17 Sep 2015. The figures are on the weak side of Asian banks throughout: CET1 of 13.5% and NSFR of 112% are below the peer median, and leverage of 4.9% and LCR of 126% are in the bottom quarter. None of the ratios has moved materially over the past four periods to 30 Jun 2026, and there has been no rating action in the last 90 days.
